walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Tienen' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140041)
walls.note: Tienen 'grote omheining' (earthen ramparts, 14th c.) as drawn on the Ferraris map (1777), with its six gates; it stood until 1781. A smaller inner wall (1537-38, 1596) also existed in 1650 and is not traced. Tienen was largely burnt by the French and Dutch in 1635 and rebuilt round the Grote Markt.

landmarks.y1650: Collegiate church with its Romanesque westwork, main bell tower of Tienen; badly burnt in 1635.
Gothic church whose nave was never built: only choir, transept and an unfinished west front stood (14th-15th c.).
Beguinage (c. 1240), burnt in 1635 and rebuilt at once.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Tienen' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140041)

landmarks.y1650: After the town hall on the Veemarkt burnt in 1635 the centre moved to the Dries, the present Grote Markt, one of the largest squares in Belgium; the present town hall is of 1836.
landmarks.src: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Tienen' (id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/306600)
